name: application-feature-flag-toggle-row
title: Feature Flag Toggle Row
description: Feature-flag management row: the flag key, environment pills (Dev/Staging/Prod), a rollout-percentage or not-enabled status line, and a trailing enable switch.
useWhen: Building an internal feature-flag or rollout-management admin panel.
Each flag needs to show which environments it's live in and its current rollout percentage at a glance.
Pairing with Preference Toggle Row's switch pattern but for engineering/ops audiences rather than end-user settings.
avoidWhen: You're building end-user notification/account preferences — use Preference Toggle Row instead, which has no environment or rollout semantics.
The flag system has more states than on/off (e.g. percentage-only rollout without a master switch) — extend the data model rather than reusing this as-is.
responsiveBehavior: Environment pills wrap onto a second line on narrow viewports while the flag key and switch stay on the first line; the switch never wraps away from the row's trailing edge.
accessibility: The flag key uses <code> since it's an identifier, not prose, giving semantic and visual (monospace) distinction.
Environment pills use both a background color and visible text ("Prod", "Staging", "Dev") so their meaning doesn't depend on color alone.
The switch is a real checkbox wrapped in a <label>, so clicking anywhere in the switch track toggles it and the checked state stays in sync with assistive technology.

variants.title: Feature Flag Toggle Row
variants.description: Three flags: new-checkout-flow (Prod+Staging, 40% rollout, on), ai-summary-panel (Staging only, off), and dark-mode-v2 (Prod+Staging+Dev, 100% rollout, on).
accessibility: Rollout percentage is always shown as text; it is never conveyed through the switch's on/off state alone.

variants.title: Feature Flag Toggle Row (Dark)
variants.description: The same three flag rows adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Environment pill colors and switch on/off states remain distinguishable at dark-surface contrast.
